english.title: Employ a disqualified person in a children's home in Wales
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) employed **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person who had been disqualified under section 68 of the Children Act 1989 from fostering a child privately, in a children's home in Wales, namely **(..SPECIFY HOME..), without disclosing to the National Assembly for Wales the fact that that person had been so disqualified and obtained that authority's written consent
english.legislation: Contrary to section 65(2) and (4) of the Children Act 1989.
english.pointstoprove:
date and Location
employ a person in a children's home in Wales
who had been disqualified from private fostering
without disclosing disqualification to authority and obtaining written consent

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Where a person contravenes subsection (2) he shall not be guilty of an offence if he proves that he did not know, and had no reasonable grounds for believing, that the person whom he was employing was disqualified under section 68
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant employed **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a person who had been disqualified from fostering a child privately, in a children's home in Wales, namely **(..SPECIFY HOME..), without disclosing to the National Assembly for Wales the fact that that person had been so disqualified and obtained that authority's written consent.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
